Looking at [Android's `export_plugin.cpp`, I found that the adaptive background icon didn't fall back to anything](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/b5bdb88062a31a982c8f3bf4b820188edd53c6c5/platform/android/export/export_plugin.cpp#L1758). After copying the `if (path.is_empty() || err != OK ...` block from the adaptive foreground icon to it like so:
```cpp
	// Adaptive background: user selection -> default.
	path = static_cast<String>(p_preset->get(LAUNCHER_ADAPTIVE_ICON_BACKGROUND_OPTION)).strip_edges();
	if (!path.is_empty()) {
		print_verbose("Loading adaptive background icon from " + path);
		background = _load_icon_or_splash_image(path, &err);
	}
	if (path.is_empty() || err != OK || background.is_null() || background->is_empty()) {
		print_verbose("- falling back to using the regular icon");
		background = icon;
	}
```

I meant try to export without XR template project.
Create a new project and do the necessary setup and then export a gradle build.
Necessary setup:

> Install the android build template. Select the menu Editor->Manage Export Templates... to download the templates. Select the menu Project->Install Android Build Template... to install the template.
I'm assuming it's an issue with your build setup because error message indicates that default icons are missing from Android build template.

Looks like that may have been it. Because I'm building from master, I had to download export templates from the Godot website, modify the version.txt file to be `4.5.dev`, place it in the corresponding folder in Godot's export templates folder. Then I was able to install the Android build template, and now a blank VR project loads successfully. Strangely, my main project crashes on startup, so I'll have to investigate that further. Hopefully I figure out what's going on with it, but if not, I suppose I can open another issue for it.

As for this "bug", it seems to me like it may have just had to do with having an out-of-date `android/build` folder. It'd be nice if there was a way to detect this and notify the user about it so that the error messages are less cryptic, but at least it doesn't seem like it's a true bug.

We do have a way to detect if the `android/build` files are outdated. `android/.build_version` file stores the version of the Android build template which detects and warns before export if it doesn't match the engine version.  `android/.build_version` shouldn't be modified manually. Also, you should always delete the older and create a new `Android build template` i.e `android/build` directory, whenever you use a different engine version.
